subject: Computing
explanation: An algorithm is a finite, ordered set of steps for solving a problem or completing a task. A computer program implements an algorithm in a programming language.

subject: Computing
explanation: Binary is a number system that uses only the digits 0 and 1. Computers use it because electronic circuits easily represent two states.

subject: Computing
explanation: A variable is a named location in memory that holds a value which can change while a program runs. Each variable usually has a data type.

subject: Computing
explanation: Recursion is when a function solves a problem by calling itself on smaller versions of the problem. It needs a base case to stop.

subject: Computing
explanation: Big O notation describes how an algorithm's running time or memory use grows as the input size grows. It ignores constant factors and focuses on the dominant term.

subject: Computing
explanation: A compiler translates the whole of a program written in a high-level language into machine code before it is run. The resulting executable runs without the compiler.

subject: Computing
explanation: A hash table stores key-value pairs and uses a hash function to decide where each pair is placed. This gives lookups in constant time on average.

subject: Computing
explanation: An API is a defined set of rules that lets one piece of software ask another for data or actions. Web APIs usually respond to HTTP requests.

subject: Computing
explanation: A Boolean is a data type with only two possible values, true or false. Conditions in if statements and loops evaluate to Booleans.

subject: Computing
explanation: A stack is a data structure where the last item added is the first one removed. Items are added with push and removed with pop.

subject: Computing
explanation: A queue is a data structure where the first item added is the first one removed. It models a waiting line.

subject: Computing
explanation: CPU stands for central processing unit. It fetches, decodes and executes the instructions of a program.

subject: Computing
explanation: A pointer is a variable whose value is the memory address of another value. Languages such as C use pointers for direct memory access.

subject: Computing
explanation: Encryption transforms readable data into unreadable ciphertext using an algorithm and a key. Only someone with the correct key can turn it back into the original.

subject: Computing
explanation: A database is an organised collection of data that can be searched and updated. Relational databases store data in linked tables.

subject: Computing
explanation: Object-oriented programming organises code into objects that combine data and the methods that act on it. Its core ideas include encapsulation, inheritance and polymorphism.

subject: Computing
explanation: Machine learning is a way of building programs that improve at a task by learning patterns from data rather than following hand-written rules. The result is a trained model.

subject: Computing
explanation: An IP address is a numerical label that identifies a device on a network and lets data be routed to it. IPv4 addresses have four numbers from 0 to 255.

subject: Computing
prompt: Which sorting algorithm repeatedly swaps adjacent elements that are out of order?
explanation: Bubble sort repeatedly steps through a list and swaps neighbouring items that are in the wrong order. It is simple but slow, with O(n^2) time in the worst case.

subject: Computing
explanation: An operating system is the software that manages a computer's hardware and provides services for other programs. Windows, macOS and Linux are examples.

subject: Computing
explanation: A loop repeats a block of code until a condition changes or a set number of repeats is done. For and while loops are common types.

subject: Computing
explanation: An if statement runs a block of code only when a condition is true. It lets a program make decisions.

subject: Computing
explanation: A subroutine is a named block of code that does a specific job and can be called from elsewhere. Using subroutines avoids repeating code.

subject: Computing
explanation: An array is a collection of items stored in order and accessed by an index number. All items usually have the same data type.

subject: Computing
explanation: A string is a data type for text: a sequence of characters. It is usually written inside quotation marks.

subject: Computing
explanation: An integer is a data type for whole numbers with no fractional part. It can be positive, negative or zero.

subject: Computing
explanation: A float is a data type for numbers with a fractional part, stored in a form of scientific notation. Calculations with floats can have small rounding errors.

subject: Computing
explanation: A syntax error is a mistake that breaks the grammar rules of a programming language. The program cannot run until it is fixed.

subject: Computing
explanation: Debugging is the process of finding and fixing errors in a program. Tools such as breakpoints and print statements help.

subject: Computing
explanation: An interpreter translates and runs a program one statement at a time instead of producing a separate executable. Python is commonly run this way.

subject: Computing
explanation: Scope is the part of a program where a variable can be used. A variable declared inside a function is usually only visible there.

subject: Computing
explanation: A global variable is declared outside any function and can be used throughout the program. Overusing them can make code harder to understand.

subject: Computing
explanation: A parameter is a value passed into a subroutine when it is called. It lets one subroutine work with different data.

subject: Computing
explanation: A linked list is a sequence of nodes, each holding a value and a reference to the next node. Items can be inserted without shifting the others.

subject: Computing
explanation: Binary search finds an item in a sorted list by repeatedly comparing with the middle item and discarding half the list. It takes about log n steps.

subject: Computing
explanation: A linear search checks each item in a list in turn until it finds the target or reaches the end. It works on unsorted lists but is slow for large ones.

subject: Computing
explanation: Merge sort splits a list in half repeatedly, sorts the pieces and merges them back together in order. It takes about n log n steps.

subject: Computing
explanation: A tree is a hierarchical data structure of nodes with a single root and branches to child nodes. Each node has one parent except the root.

subject: Computing
explanation: A graph is a data structure of nodes joined by edges. It models networks such as roads, friendships or the internet.

subject: Computing
explanation: Abstraction means hiding unnecessary detail and keeping only what matters to solve a problem. A map is an abstraction of a landscape.

subject: Computing
explanation: Decomposition is breaking a large problem into smaller, easier parts that can be solved separately. It makes complex programs manageable.

subject: Computing
explanation: Pseudocode is a way of writing an algorithm in structured, plain language that is not tied to any programming language. It is used to plan code.

subject: Computing
explanation: A flowchart is a diagram that shows the steps of an algorithm using standard symbols joined by arrows. Diamonds show decisions.

subject: Computing
explanation: A truth table lists every possible combination of inputs to a logic expression and the resulting output. It fully describes how a logic gate behaves.

subject: Computing
explanation: An AND gate outputs true only when both of its inputs are true. Otherwise its output is false.

subject: Computing
explanation: A NOT gate has one input and outputs the opposite value. True becomes false and false becomes true.

subject: Computing
explanation: A bit is a single binary digit, either 0 or 1. It is the smallest unit of data in a computer.

subject: Computing
explanation: A byte is a group of eight bits. It is the standard unit for measuring storage and can represent 256 different values.

subject: Computing
explanation: Hexadecimal is a number system with 16 digits, 0 to 9 and A to F. It is a compact way of writing binary values.

subject: Computing
explanation: ASCII is a character encoding that gives each letter, digit and symbol a number. The original version uses 7 bits to represent 128 characters.

subject: Computing
explanation: A pixel is the smallest single point of a digital image or screen. Many pixels together form the picture.

subject: Computing
explanation: RAM is the computer's fast, temporary working memory. It holds the programs and data in use and is cleared when power is switched off.

subject: Computing
explanation: A cache is a small, very fast store that keeps copies of frequently used data. It reduces the time spent fetching data from slower memory.

subject: Computing
explanation: A router forwards data packets between networks, such as from a home network to the internet. It decides the best route for each packet.

subject: Computing
explanation: A firewall monitors network traffic and blocks anything that breaks its security rules. It protects a computer or network from unauthorised access.

subject: Computing
explanation: Phishing is sending fake messages that pretend to be from a trusted source to trick people into giving away passwords or other private information.

subject: Computing
explanation: Malware is software designed to damage a computer or steal information. Viruses, worms and ransomware are all types of malware.

subject: Computing
explanation: Version control is a system that records changes to files over time so earlier versions can be recovered. It also lets many people work on the same code.

subject: Computing
explanation: HTTP is the protocol browsers and servers use to exchange web pages and data. A browser sends a request and the server sends back a response.

subject: Computing
explanation: URL stands for uniform resource locator. It is the address that identifies a resource on the web.

subject: Computing
explanation: A keyboard is used to type letters, numbers and commands into a computer.

subject: Computing
explanation: A computer mouse moves a pointer on the screen and lets you click on things.

subject: Computing
explanation: A password is a secret word or phrase that keeps an account safe. Never share it with anyone except a trusted adult.

subject: Computing
explanation: Saving stores your work on a computer or online so you can open it again later.

subject: Computing
explanation: A printer puts words and pictures from a computer onto paper.

subject: Computing
explanation: A sequence is a set of instructions that must happen in the right order, like the steps for brushing your teeth.

subject: Computing

subject: Computing
explanation: Repetition means doing the same instructions again and again. In code, a repeat block saves writing the same steps many times.

subject: Computing

subject: Computing
explanation: An output is what a computer gives back, like a picture on the screen or a sound from a speaker.

subject: Computing

subject: Computing

subject: Computing

subject: Computing
explanation: A search engine helps you find web pages. You type in some words and it shows a list of results.

subject: Computing

subject: Computing
explanation: A camera takes photos and videos. Many computers and tablets have one built in for video calls.

subject: Computing
explanation: Debugging means finding and fixing the mistakes in a program or set of instructions.
